description: Dated implementation observations, separate from the frozen research catalog and upstream CIP status. Publication describes source availability; capability environment and evidence describe what was actually exercised.

records.title: State Capsules
records.summary: A local state-history composer and experimental Plutus lifecycle with separate evidence for issuance and later state changes.

capabilities.title: Compose and verify a local history
capabilities.description: Create datum states, advance a hash-linked sequence and export a frozen branch. The browser history has no chain authority.

capabilities.title: Evaluate one-shot issuance
capabilities.description: An unsigned pair mint using current public inputs passed independent node script evaluation; missing-signer and reference-only seed variants were rejected.

capabilities.title: Exercise evolution and freeze
capabilities.description: Compiled script wrappers exercised complete synthetic issuance, evolution and freeze transactions. This is local evaluator evidence.

capabilities.title: Fixed contract parameters with Aiken equivalence checks
capabilities.description: Apply an explicit transaction output reference and 1–28 UTF-8-byte base name to the pinned PlutusV3 capsule blueprint. Locally tested applied scripts and policy identities match Aiken across 256 generated cases and CSL 17 independently; seed existence, unspentness and contract spending are not checked.

capabilities.title: Local browser contract parameter review and export
capabilities.description: The Contract compiler Lab accepts the explicit seed/name, clears old output when any input changes, and exports applied blueprint and identity bytes. Local browser evidence covers 256 compiler-oracle cases plus 15 integrated desktop/mobile UI checks. No wallet or transaction is prepared.

evidence.description: Published browser composer and local verifier.
Shared datum and history codec used by the browser and local tooling.
Combined issuance/spending source; its rules require the intended applied script identity.
Lifecycle, irreversible freeze/ADA behavior and scoped readiness.
Receipt: 256 serializer/hash fixtures, 258 history states and 34 rejection cases.
Receipt: five complete synthetic signed transactions and compiled wrapper evaluation, with explicit phase-1 and inclusion exclusions.
Sanitized unsigned issuance evaluation receipt, including two negative cases; no transaction was submitted.

Fixed-blueprint parameter application using pinned Harmonic UPLC libraries. Accepts one explicit seed reference and an exact UTF-8 base name; returns script bytes, hashes and labeled token names without a wallet or transaction.
Parameterizer scope, fixed blueprint/compiler identities, primary application sources, exact UTF-8 and strict input limits, Aiken/CSL comparisons, and explicit absence of a live capsule mint flow.

Local compiler oracle receipt: 256 generated parameter pairs, 512 Aiken CLI invocations and 768 handler-byte comparisons; complete applied blueprints and independent CSL 17 script hashes agree. This is compiler equivalence testing, not independent Cardano node evaluation.
Local Chromium receipt: the same 256 Aiken-oracle cases and 768 handler-byte comparisons pass without Node globals, external requests or wallet APIs. The recorded 442 ms describes one local run only.

Published browser audit procedure. A developer-observed local run passed 15 checks at 1440 and 390 pixels, including exact exports, UTF-8 identity, invalid inputs, no wallet/runtime network operations and stale lazy-import cancellation. The timestamp comes from the local report; this source pin is a procedure, not a published or authenticated run receipt.

limits: No capsule mint, confirmation, authentic on-chain history or device-wallet acceptance is established.
Independent node evidence covers issuance only; evolution and freeze evidence is synthetic and local.
Permanent freeze locks reference state and ADA; no recovery, withdrawal, unfreeze or issuer override exists.

Parameterization is limited to the embedded blueprint identified by its hash and local exact-byte equivalence tests. It is not a general Aiken compiler, a security audit, a seed-availability check, a new node evaluation or a capsule wallet mint flow.
nextEvidence: Complete wallet lifecycle with preproduction inclusion and state recovery.
External security review and explicit loss/freeze UX.
A separately reviewed capsule transaction and wallet workflow that consumes the exact parameterized identity, plus independent node evaluation of its real lifecycle before any deployment claim.

records.title: Agent mint requests and MCP
records.summary: A public nine-tool service for content requests and unsigned native transactions, with a separately installed Node signature-verification package.

capabilities.title: Prepare content for visible review
capabilities.description: The dated endpoint check found nine tools and 55 resources. Knowledge lookup, intent roundtrips, proof matching and tamper rejection passed with modern and legacy clients.

capabilities.title: Import an agent request
capabilities.description: The browser verifies exact embedded files, then asks the user to continue into its existing wallet review. The intent itself contains no wallet address or transaction.

capabilities.title: Prepare unsigned native transactions
capabilities.description: The installable Node service shares the actual native builder and verifies external witness sets against its retained preparation. It exposes no signing or submission tool.

capabilities.title: Prepare an unsigned NFT or data transaction
capabilities.description: Both official client eras prepared synthetic NFT/data transactions on the hosted Worker. Independent local checks matched body hashes, exact metadata, output destinations and ADA/token conservation. No signatures or chain inclusion were checked.

evidence.description: Actual public clients in both protocol eras observed nine tools and 55 resources. Synthetic NFT/data transactions passed independent hash, metadata, output and ADA/token conservation checks; no real wallet or submission.
Public versus Node capability boundaries, explicit-byte privacy, review flow and reproducible checks.
Published nine-tool public Worker with stateless native unsigned preparation and fixed public protocol reads.
Published Node factory, shared builder, stored review context and external witness verification.
Strict bounded content packet and verification, shared by client and MCP.
Visible import/inspect/continue interface and public connection instructions.
Public Streamable HTTP observation: eight tools, 55 resources, content/intent/proof checks and origin rejection; no wallet access or chain submission.
Stateless adapter for the shared native builder, with explicit snapshot, output and evidence boundaries.

limits: The public endpoint receives explicit file bytes; browser-local hashing is required when originals must stay on the device.
The unsigned public tool receives an explicitly supplied wallet snapshot. It does not connect a wallet, retain preparation, sign, submit or verify external witnesses.
Both public and Node preparation rely on caller-supplied UTxOs; their current unspent chain state and ownership are not independently established by preparation.
No new mainnet mint or wallet-device acceptance is established by the synthetic SDK/browser checks. Native quantity one is not a lifetime supply cap.
nextEvidence: Recheck the live endpoint after deployments; retain dated receipts rather than treating this observation as permanent freshness.
Observe real-device wallet acceptance separately from SDK and synthetic browser checks.

records.title: Standards Observatory
records.summary: A source-pinned research catalog, searchable public interface and read-only monitor that reports upstream CIP drift without changing claims.

capabilities.title: Search the pinned research snapshot
capabilities.description: The 53-entry catalog remains research-only; implementation evidence belongs in this separate register.

capabilities.title: Compare one immutable upstream revision
capabilities.description: A live sample compared 40 pinned CIP artifacts at one resolved upstream commit: 40 unchanged, zero errors, ten non-CIP sources skipped.

capabilities.title: Produce a review report artifact
capabilities.description: The published workflow definition supports manual and weekly checks with contents-read permission and report artifacts. No successful scheduled run is asserted here.

evidence.description: Pure bounded validation and literal search over the immutable research catalog.
Published standards search and source detail interface.
Fixed official-CIPs origin, one upstream HEAD resolution, bounded transport and immutable report links.
Dated source-drift receipt; the sample is not a perpetual freshness assertion.
Scope, incomplete/error handling and explicit review/admission process.
Artifact-only scheduled/manual workflow definition; execution remains a separate observation.

limits: No catalog mutation, CIP-status promotion, dependency update or automatic implementation admission occurs.
Only the pinned official-CIPs paths are compared; new CIPs, external linked files and the ten tool repositories are not monitored.
An HTTP error or missing source does not establish withdrawal. The pinned sample cannot establish present freshness.
nextEvidence: Review changed primary text before revising affected catalog summaries.
Record later monitor runs and separately scope any expansion to tool releases or wallet interoperability.

records.title: Artifact Passport
records.summary: A published exact-payload receipt adapter, browser composer and offline verifier with separate content and transaction evidence.

capabilities.title: Export a portable content passport
capabilities.description: Adapt supported NFT/data receipts, recover exact embedded bytes, bind optional supplied transaction bytes and preserve source/build statements as declarations.

capabilities.title: Reject ambiguous and oversized evidence
capabilities.description: Eight local test groups include actual shared-builder receipts, CBOR preflight before WASM, exact round trips, byte-view bounds and caller-method rejection. Tests are developer observations, not inclusion evidence.

evidence.description: Published adapter and pure verifier.
Developer-observed eight-group pass, including actual shared NFT/data builder receipts. Artifact identifies the test procedure, not a chain receipt.
Published profile scope, deterministic JSON/byte rules and explicit nonclaims.
Two synthetic public fixtures also passed the independent Python SHA-256/BLAKE2b oracle.
Published browser import, canonical export and per-claim evidence view.

Developer-observed public browser flow: creation, canonical export, offline reopen, optional original-transaction check, changed evidence rejection and Activity recovery. Artifact identifies the test procedure; no real wallet or chain submission occurred.

limits: Source and browser availability do not establish a passport MCP tool or any chain observation.
A content checksum is not an authenticated receipt. Inclusion, signatures, authorship, ownership, rights and build reproduction remain unverified.
The profile supports exact-payload NFT/data receipts only; legacy artwork, games, Scroll/Book and arbitrary CIP-68 records are outside this adapter.
nextEvidence: Specify separate adapters before extending the profile to additional Studio artifact formats.
Independently observe chain inclusion or build execution before adding those claims.

records.title: Holder-proof verifier
records.summary: Published experimental source for offline signature-and-holdings verification with injected trusted adapters; no authentication service is deployed.

capabilities.title: Verify the exact signed challenge
capabilities.description: Preserve protected COSE bytes, require Ed25519 headers/key parameters, apply strict verification and bind the payment key to the exact challenge address.

capabilities.title: Compose a scoped observed-point decision
capabilities.description: Check origin, action, network, resource, session, expiry, fresh trusted snapshot and atomic single-process nonce consumption. The result is valid only at the reported observation.

capabilities.title: Bound direct byte-array entry points
capabilities.description: Eleven regression groups cover native byte slots, offset Buffers, overridden methods and shared/detached memory. No caller callback executed in those tests.

evidence.description: Candidate cryptographic verifier; no wallet, signing or provider calls.
Candidate composition with server-owned configuration, challenge store and trusted snapshot adapter.

Scoped evidence: 52 primitive checks, 17 accepted COSE cases, two crypto diagnostics, 84 named rejections, 23 composition checks, mutation/truncation cases and 16 independently verified public fixtures.
Developer-observed eleven-group direct-input pass. This artifact is the test procedure, not a live authorization receipt.

limits: No HTTP endpoint, protected-object delivery, real chain adapter, real-wallet interoperability or production nonce store is implemented here.
Holding, canonicality and freshness are trusted adapter observations, not cryptographic chain-inclusion proofs.
Memory nonce consumption is single-process only; production storage needs durable atomic expiry/session checks at commit time.
No external security audit or future/exclusive holding guarantee is established.
nextEvidence: Independently review a real chain adapter, durable session/nonce storage and protected delivery before any authentication deployment.
Observe actual wallet compatibility before claiming support for named wallets or devices.

records.title: Exact music release packages, native preparation and receipt recovery
records.summary: Published Studio music extension with exact audio/cover bytes and declared credits, a dedicated browser wallet-review path, strict recovery from transaction metadata, and locally tested package-only MCP tools. Evidence is local or synthetic; public deployment and chain inclusion are separate observations.

capabilities.title: Exact music files and credit package composition
capabilities.description: Compose one cover and 1–7 audio files with release, artist and credit data; export and reopen a canonical music package whose hash binds every exact file byte and supported declaration. The local browser run passed seven integrated groups; metadata codec fixtures cover three roundtrips, 56 malformed composers and 128 checksum mutations.

capabilities.title: Shared native builder preserving committed credits
capabilities.description: The dedicated music entry point uses the existing Studio constructor, derives asset identity from the full package commitment and preserves its exact music metadata. Ten synthetic integration groups cover credit changes, ADA/assets, signatures, fees and complete size; six ordinary NFT/data preparation baselines remain byte-identical.

capabilities.title: Local browser review and exact transaction-metadata recovery
capabilities.description: The Music Lab passes its full package into explicit wallet review and Activity routes actual music CBOR to strict credit/file recovery, including receipts with stripped sidecars. Synthetic browser checks cover receipt-before-submit, stale signing prompts, storage failure and uncertain submission. Eleven recovery groups reject 82 malformed/mismatched cases; imported confirmation remains a receipt-reported declaration.

capabilities.title: Locally tested bot music-package preparation and verification
capabilities.description: create_music_release and verify_music_release return the same canonical package, its hash, metadata-only budget and a fixed Music Lab review URL. Six music-specific test groups ran within the 37-group local MCP suite and its clean install, using official modern/legacy clients on Node and Workerd. The local Worker exposed 12 tools; Node exposed 14, with 61 resources; these counts are local test observations, not a public deployment receipt.

evidence.description: Strict pure music profile, bounded inert composer values, canonical package commitment, exact embedded-file metadata, independent CBOR writer and exact credit/file reconstruction.

Shared ordinary/music native construction plus current review and signature checks. The explicit trusted music branch preserves credits without accepting arbitrary metadata callbacks or extending ordinary mint intents.
Bounded offline receipt routing and recovery through CSL 17. Derives actual mint and metadata identities and rejects mismatches; reported receipt state is distinct from checked local content.
Published browser composer, full package import/export and dedicated musicPackage wallet-review handoff. Draft changes invalidate the prepared package and its open review.

CIP-60-aligned Studio extension and primary-source adapter boundary: exact chunked file URIs, required/optional credits and metadata Boolean/CDDL conflicts. Its original codec-kit wallet/MCP omissions are historical; later builder, receipt and service sources in this record provide their separate scope.

Published deterministic codec measurements for three original synthetic roundtrips; the associated verifier documents 285 assertions and independent CSL/Python CBOR and hash agreement. These fixtures do not establish a real recording duration, rights or player support.

Ten-group synthetic builder evidence, including six unchanged ordinary baselines. The small fixture measures 6,844 metadata bytes and 7,380 complete signed bytes; a 13,717-byte metadata package rejects a fragmented wallet at full signed-size validation. Original fixture flags describe the pre-UI/pre-MCP adapter kit, not later source availability.

Eleven-group strict recovery fixture evidence with 82 rejected cases, exact package identity and byte measurements. All inputs and signatures are synthetic; provider requests and chain submissions are zero.

Published browser audit procedure. A developer-observed local run passed seven integrated groups covering canonical exports, changed credits, synthetic signing and conservation, receipt routing, pending-prompt cancellation, storage failure and uncertain submission. The timestamp is the local log modification time; the source pin identifies the procedure, not a published/authenticated run receipt.

Strict package-only MCP schemas and handlers call the trusted shared codec, preserve inert credit links without fetching them, and return a fixed Music Lab review handoff. They neither construct a music transaction nor change the ordinary mint-intent schema.

Bot package contract, canonical export/import instructions, declared-link treatment, metadata-only budget, local tool/resource checks and explicit separation from unsigned transactions, wallet authority and public deployment.

Published six-group music MCP test procedure. Developer-observed full local and clean-install MCP runs both passed 37 groups against 58 entries, 73 sources and 61 resources. This includes Node/Workerd and modern/legacy SDK lanes; the timestamp is the clean log modification time, not a deployed-service or authenticated test receipt.

limits: This is the cip60-v3-studio-exact-files extension, not strict CIP-60 v3 CDDL conformance or demonstrated wallet/player interoperability. Research maturity and upstream CIP status are unchanged.
Audio/cover bytes and metadata declarations are committed; authorship, assignment of identifiers, copyright, share entitlement, royalty payments, recording duration and ownership are not verified.

A 14,000-byte music metadata cap leaves no guaranteed complete transaction headroom. The browser still needs fresh wallet/protocol inputs, full transaction sizing, fee checks and explicit human signing review.

MCP tools only prepare or verify a music package; they do not prepare a music transaction, fetch declared links/media, persist packages, authenticate users, sign, submit or verify chain inclusion. The fixed browser review URL is a handoff, not evidence of a deployed service.
All observed wallet interactions and signed transactions in these tests are synthetic. No live music mint, public music service deployment or chain confirmation is established by this record.

Receipt recovery checks exact local transaction content. Payment-signature validity, complete ledger validity, inclusion, confirmation, ownership and rights remain unchecked; a receipt state stays an unverified declaration.
Ordinary mint intents reject music packages. The existing Artifact Passport profile continues to reject music metadata; generic exact-file recovery alone is not credit verification.
nextEvidence: A separately dated live-service receipt for the deployed 12-tool release using the official MCP client, exact package checks and the admitted implementation-register resource.
An explicitly authorized real-wallet test lifecycle with known transaction inclusion and independent exact-file plus credit recovery; distinguish network, wallet and provider observations.
Documented independent consumer/player interoperability tests and an explicit reviewed adapter for any broader CIP-60 or Artifact Passport profile.
